verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要使耶路撒冷知道她那些可憎的事，
verses.en: “Son of man, confront Jerusalem[NOTE:1] with her abominable practices
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
16:2 "Son of man" This phrase is a literary marker of a new topic or new revelation. See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "make known" The VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil
IMPERATIVE) means "to announce." The Niphal stem is often used of making
YHWH known (cf. Ezek. 20:5,9; 38:23; 35:11) and also in the Hiphil (cf. Ezek. 39:7). However, in
this context it means declaring to Jerusalem her "abominations." YHWH made Himself and His will clear to
His people, but they would not draw near to Him and follow Him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 说主耶和华对耶路撒冷如此说：你根本，你出世，是在迦南地；你父亲是亚摩利人，你母亲是赫人。
verses.en: and say, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
verses.commentary:
16:3 "origin" This term (BDB 468) occurs only three times in the OT and are all in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 16:3;
21:30; 29:14). The etymology is uncertain.

- The same letters can mean "a kind of weapon" (cf. Gen. 49:5).

- Some scholars think the meaning is related to the VERB (BDB 468 II)
"dig" or "hew" (cf. Ps. 22:16).

- Others think it is from BDB 500 II, "to get by trade" or "purchase."

▣ "Your origin and your birth are from the land of the Canaanite" This could be understood in several senses.

- This explains the source of their idolatrous tendencies

- They were not a people until YHWH chose them and delivered them from Egypt

- from the land of Canaan (idolatrous tendencies)

- father was an Amorite, Ezek. 16:45

- mother was a Hittite, Ezek. 16:45

- refers exclusively to the physical city of Salem, Jebus, and later Jerusalem

The term "father" may refer to tribal ancestors (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 219) and not Abraham, who
is called "a wandering Aramean" in Deut. 26:5. This verse is figurative, meaning that Judah's parents were
non-Israelite. This was revealed by their idolatrous actions. This is not a text on genealogy, but on idolatry!
Israel was unfaithful from the very beginning (cf. Deut. 32:5; Isa. 1:2-3; Jer. 7:24-26; 11:7-8; Ezek. 2:6-8;
3:9,26; 12:2-3; 16:3,45; Hosea 6:7; 9:10; 11:1-4; 13:4-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, ZION, JERUSALEM

▣ "Canaanite" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE, C. #8

verses.zh: 论到你出世的景况，在你初生的日子没有为你断脐带，也没有用水洗你，使你洁净，丝毫没有撒盐在你身上，也没有用布裹你。
verses.en: As for your birth, on the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, nor were you washed in water;[NOTE:1] you were certainly not rubbed down with salt, nor wrapped with blankets.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in water you were not washed for cleansing” or “with water you were not washed smooth” (see D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:473, n. 57, for a discussion of possible meanings of this hapax legomenon).
Arab midwives still cut the umbilical cords of infants and then proceed to apply salt and oil to their bodies.
verses.commentary:
16:4-5 These verses describe, in birthing symbolism, Israel's predicament at birth without YHWH's help.

- the umbilical cord was not cut

- they were not washed with water for cleansing

- they were not rubbed with salt

- they were not wrapped in cloths (this was meant to protect the limbs, the opposite of squirming, cf.
Ezek. 16:6)

- no eye looked on them with pity

- there was no compassion on them

- they were thrown out into the open field (female babies were sometimes abandoned in the Ancient Near East)

Israel was neglected and abandoned by all! None of the traditional birthing rites were observed! Death
was certain!

Numbers 1-4 detail practices of Arab groups, which are still present in Palestine today. It would
have been the expected procedures for a "wanted" child.

16:4 "washed with water for cleansing" The word "cleansing" (BDB 606, KB 650) is found only here and its meaning is unknown.

verses.zh: 谁的眼也不可怜你，为你做一件这样的事怜恤你；但你初生的日子扔在田野，是因你被厌恶。
verses.en: No eye took pity on you to do even one of these things for you to spare you;[NOTE:1] you were thrown out into the open field[NOTE:2] because you were detested on the day you were born.
notes: These verbs, “pity” and “spare,” echo the judgment oracles in 5:11; 7:4, 9; 8:18; 9:5, 10.
A similar concept is found in Deut 32:10.
verses.commentary:
16:5 "abhorred" This NOUN (BDB 172) appears only here in the OT. However, the VERB is
used in Ezek. 16:45 (BDB 171, KB 199, Qal PARTICIPLE and Qal PERFECT) twice. It
denotes something hated because it is unclean (i.e. dung or spoilage).

Much of Ezekiel's terminology is drawn from Leviticus 26. In this chapter this word is used of
both Israel and YHWH.

- Israel

- they abhorred YHWH's commandments, Ezek. 16:15

- they abhorred YHWH's commandments, Ezek. 16:43

- YHWH

- YHWH will not abhor them, Ezek. 16:11

- YHWH abhors them because of their idolatry, Ezek. 16:30

- YHWH abhors them because of their covenant disobedience, Ezek. 16:44

Leviticus 26 is parallel to Deut. 28:15-68.

verses.zh: 「我从你旁边经过，见你滚在血中，就对你说：你虽在血中，仍可存活；你虽在血中，仍可存活。
verses.en: “‘I passed by you and saw you kicking around helplessly in your blood. I said to you as you lay there in your blood, “Live!” I said to you as you lay there in your blood, “Live!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The translation reflects the Hebrew text, which repeats the statement, perhaps for emphasis. However, a few medieval Hebrew manuscripts, the Old Greek, and the Syriac do not include the repetition. The statement could have been accidentally repeated, or the second occurrence could have been accidentally omitted. Based on the available evidence it is difficult to know which is more likely.
verses.commentary:
16:6-14 This describes YHWH's loving acts toward Israel.

- saw her predicament and commanded life (two Qal IMPERATIVES,
BDB 310, KB 309), Ezek. 16:6

- made her numerous, like the plants of the field, Ezek. 16:7

- Israel grew like a young woman to maturity (full height, full breasts, long hair or pubic hair), but was
uncared for (i.e. naked and bare). YHWH proposed to her and made promises to her (i.e. marriage covenant),
Ezek. 16:7-8

- bathed with water, Ezek. 16:9

- anointed with oil, Ezek. 16:9

- clothed, Ezek. 16:10

- put shoes on her feet, Ezek. 16:10

- wrapped in fine shawl, Ezek. 16:10

- gave jewelry, Ezek. 16:11-13a

- gave good food, Ezek. 16:13b

- her beauty was renowned because of YHWH's care and gifts, Ezek. 16:14

She was nothing, yea despised, until YHWH chose her, cared for her, and married her
(i.e. "swore," BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal IMPERFECT).

16:6

NASB, TEV
"squirming"

NKJV
"struggling"

NRSV
"flailing about"

NJB, REB, NET
"kicking"

Peshitta, JPSOA
"wallowing"

LXX
"polluted"

The term (BDB 100, KB 115, Hithpolel PARTICIPLE)
normally means "to tread down" or "trample," but in the Hithpolel stem (here and v. 22) it seems to
refer to the random movement of an infant's limbs.

verses.zh: 我使你生长好像田间所长的，你就渐渐长大，以致极其俊美，两乳成形，头发长成，你却仍然赤身露体。
verses.en: I made you plentiful like sprouts in a field; you grew tall and came of age so that you could wear jewelry. Your breasts had formed and your hair had grown, but you were still naked and bare.
verses.commentary:
16:7

NASB
"numerous"

NKJV
"thrive"

NRSV, LXX
"grow up"

TEV, NJB, JPSOA
"grow"

Peshitta
"multiply"

"A myriad" (BDB 914) literally refers to ten thousand, but it is often used in a figurative sense
(i.e. Gen. 24:60; Ps. 3:6; Song of Songs 5:10).

▣ "You grew up" (BDB 915, KB 1176, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw) means "become a numerous people" (i.e. Gen. 1:28; 9:1-7; Exod. 1:10,12,20;
Deut. 6:3; 8:1; 30:16).

- BDB suggests that here it means "grow great" or "grow strong," from an Aramean root (NASB, Peshitta)

- KB suggests "grow up" for the meaning here (NRSV, TEV, NJB, LXX)

- It is a word play on "numerous" (רבה, BDB 915), which means "myriad"
(רבבה, BDB 914), found at the beginning of v. 7

NASB
"reached the age for fine ornaments"

NKJV
"became very beautiful"

NRSV, REB
"arrived at full womanhood"

TEV
"became a young woman"

NJB
"reached marriageable age"

JPSOA
"your tiime for love had arrived"

Peshitta
"your had reached marriage age"

This is literally "with ornament of ornaments" (BDB 725 CONSTRUCT BDB 725). This phrase and
the next two mean she had reached an age to be married (RSV, NEB).

The UBS Text Project, p. 40, gives two translation options based on textual variants.

- "to the beauty of beauties" (lit. "jewellery" doubled, BDB 725, KB 791 II)

- "in the time of menstruations" (emendation)

- JPSOA footnote, "meaning of Hebrew uncertain"

verses.zh: 我从你旁边经过，看见你的时候正动爱情，便用衣襟搭在你身上，遮盖你的赤体；又向你起誓，与你结盟，你就归于我。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: “‘Then I passed by you and watched you, noticing[NOTE:1] that you had reached the age for love.[NOTE:2] I spread my cloak[NOTE:3] over you and covered your nakedness. I swore a solemn oath to you and entered into a marriage covenant with you, declares the Sovereign Lord, and you became mine.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a participle.
See similar use of this term in Ezek 23:17; Prov 7:16; Song of Songs 4:10; 7:13.
Heb “wing” or “skirt.” The gesture symbolized acquiring a woman in early Arabia (similarly, see Deut 22:30; Ruth 3:9).

verses.zh: 那时我用水洗你，洗净你身上的血，又用油抹你。
verses.en: “‘Then I bathed you in water, washed the blood off you, and anointed you with fragrant oil.
verses.commentary:
16:9 This describes what the prospective husband (YHWH) did for His wife-to-be.

- bath of cleansing, still done before the wedding rite

- blood washed off, this refers to her menstrual period, denoting she is of marriageable age and not pregnant (this may also be implied in Ezek. 16:7)

- anointed with oil, preparation for the wedding feast

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

verses.zh: 我也使你身穿绣花衣服，脚穿海狗皮鞋，并用细麻布给你束腰，用丝绸为衣披在你身上，
verses.en: I dressed you in embroidered clothing and put fine leather sandals on your feet. I wrapped you with fine linen and covered you with silk.
verses.commentary:
16:10 "embroidered cloth" This term (BDB 955) is used several times in Ezekiel of expensive multi-colored
or embroidered cloth (cf. Ezek. 16:10,13,18; 26:16; 27:7,16,24). It is used in Ezek. 17:3 to describe a
multi-colored great eagle.

NASB
"porpoise skin"

NKJV
"badger skin"

NRSV, NJB, NET
"fine leather"

TEV
"of the best leather"

REB
"dugong-hide"

JPSOA
"dolphin leather"

The term (BDB 1065, KB 1720 I) refers to a type of animal skin. Exactly which animal is uncertain.

- dolphin, Arabic (JPSOA, NASB in Exod. 25:5)

- sheep, conjecture

- leather, Egyptian (NRSV, NJB, NET, "fine leather," KB's best guess)

- seal, NASB, Exod. 35:23

Elsewhere, this term is used for the construction of the tabernacle (cf. Exod. 25:5; 26:14;
35:7,23; 36:19; 39:34; Num. 4:6,8). The best choices seem to be #1 or #4, both found in the Red Sea in large
numbers having skins large enough to make durable sheeting for the tabernacle.

▣ "fine linen" The etymology of this word (BDB 1058, KB 1663 III, B) is uncertain (JPSOA). Most scholars relate it to an
Egyptian word for fine woven linen JPSOA.

- for fine garments, Gen. 41:42; Prov. 31:22

- for sails, Ezek. 16:10,13; 27:7

- for priestly garments, Exod. 28:5,39

- for hangings in the tabernacle, Exod. 27:9,16,18; 38:9,16,18

- for curtains in the tabernacle, Exod. 26:1,31,36; 36:8,35,37

16:12-13a This is a list of jewelry expressing YHWH's love and care for Israel.

- ornaments, Ezek. 16:11, BDB 725

- bracelets, Ezek. 16:11, BDB 855

- chain (necklace), Ezek. 16:11, BDB 914, cf. Gen. 41:42

- ring in your nose, Ezek. 16:12, BDB 633, cf. Gen. 24:47; Isa. 3:21

- earrings, Ezek. 16:12, BDB 722, cf. Num. 31:50

- crown of beauty, Ezek. 16:12, BDB 742

- adorned with gold and silver, Ezek. 16:13

verses.zh: 又用妆饰打扮你，将镯子戴在你手上，将金链戴在你项上。
verses.en: I adorned you with jewelry. I put bracelets on your hands and a necklace around your neck.

verses.zh: 我也将环子戴在你鼻子上，将耳环戴在你耳朵上，将华冠戴在你头上。
verses.en: I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.

verses.zh: 这样，你就有金银的妆饰，穿的是细麻衣和丝绸，并绣花衣；吃的是细面、蜂蜜，并油。你也极其美貌，发达到王后的尊荣。
verses.en: You were adorned with gold and silver, while your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidery. You ate the finest flour, honey, and olive oil. You became extremely beautiful and attained the position of royalty.
verses.commentary:
16:13 "exceedingly beautiful" The ADVERB "exceedingly" comes from a
repetition of BDB 547, cf. Ezek. 9:9; Gen. 17:2,6,20; Exod. 1:7.

▣ "advanced to royalty" This orphan child (i.e. Israel) is elevated to the royal family status,
both by adoption and marriage.

verses.zh: 你美貌的名声传在列邦中，你十分美貌，是因我加在你身上的威荣。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Your fame[NOTE:1] spread among the nations because of your beauty; your beauty was perfect because of the splendor that I bestowed on you, declares the Sovereign Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “name.”
The description of the nation Israel in vv. 10-14 recalls the splendor of the nation’s golden age under King Solomon.
verses.commentary:
16:14 "it was perfect" This ADJECTIVE (BDB 483) is used in the sense of
wholeness or an entire state of completion. It is used

- of the report of Jerusalem's beauty, 16:14; Ps. 50:2; Lam. 2:15

- of the King of Tyre, 27:3; 28:12

verses.zh: 只是你仗着自己的美貌，又因你的名声就行邪淫。你纵情淫乱，使过路的任意而行。
verses.en: “‘But you trusted in your beauty and capitalized on your fame by becoming a prostitute. You offered your sexual favors to every man who passed by so that your beauty[NOTE:1] became his.
notes: Heb “it” (so KJV, ASV); the referent (the beauty in which the prostitute trusted; see the beginning of the verse) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
16:15 "you trusted in your beauty" This VERB (BDB 105, KB 120, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) basically meant
"trust" or "rely upon." In this context it denotes Judah's reliance on fertility idolatry (cf. Ps. 115:4-8;
135:15-18; Isa. 42:17; Jer. 13:25; 48:7).

▣ "played the harlot" This VERB (BDB 275, KB 275, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw) means "commit fornication." Idolatry is imagery for sexual
unfaithfulness (cf. Ezek. 16:28; 23:30; Jer. 3:1). Israel and Judah were married to
YHWH (cf. Ezek. 16:8), but they pursued the gods of Egypt, Canaan, Assyria, and Babylon. This could have
been done in one of two ways.

- official governmental relations (i.e. treaties) which were done in the name of these national gods
(cf. Ezek. 16:26,28; 23:5,7; Isa. 23:17)

- the worship of these foreign gods (cf. chapter 8; Exod. 34:15-16; Lev. 20:5; Deut. 31:16)

This sexual (marriage, cf. Hosea 1-3; Eph. 5:21-31) imagery is used because of the personal nature of faith.
Marriage is often used as a way of referring to intimacy. Faith is a spiritual intimacy! YHWH takes human commitment (i.e. free will) seriously.

See a brief discussion of prostitution in the ANE in IVP Bible Background Commentary, p. 702.

verses.zh: 你用衣服为自己在高处结彩，在其上行邪淫。这样的事将来必没有，也必不再行了。
verses.en: You took some of your clothing and made for yourself decorated high places; you engaged in prostitution on them. You went to him to become his.[NOTE:1]
notes: The text as written in the MT is incomprehensible (“not coming [plural] and he will not”). Driver has suggested a copying error of similar-sounding words, specifically לֹא (loʾ) for לוֹ (lo). The feminine participle בָאוֹת (vaʾot) has also been read as the feminine perfect בָאת (vaʾt). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:228, n. 15.b, and D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:486, n. 137.
verses.commentary:
16:16-21 The apostasy of Jerusalem took Judah's beauty and wealth given to her by YHWH (cf. Ezek. 16:10-14)
and turned it into pagan shrines and worship practices.

- decorated shrines ("high places," cf. Ezek. 16:24,31,39) of multi-colored cloth, given by YHWH,
used as a place to commit adultery

- made idols with ornaments and jewels given by YHWH, Ezek. 16:17

- offered YHWH's oil and incense, Ezek. 16:18

- offered YHWH's food, Ezek. 16:19

- offered the fruit of the womb (i.e. children, Ezek. 16:36), which YHWH had bestowed, Ezek. 16:20-22.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH

verses.zh: 你又将我所给你那华美的金银、宝器为自己制造人像，与他行邪淫；
verses.en: You also took your beautiful jewelry, made of my gold and my silver I had given to you, and made for yourself male images and engaged in prostitution[NOTE:1] with them.
notes: Or perhaps “and worshiped them,” if the word “prostitution” is understood in a figurative rather than a literal sense (cf. CEV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
16:17 "made for yourself male images" These could refer to phallic statues (i.e. Ba'al) or jewelry. The gold and
silver were YHWH's gifts to His bride (Israel). They turned these gifts into fertility idols (like the golden calf of Exodus 32), just as they
turned the beautiful clothing given by YHWH into mats and blankets on which to fornicate (cf. Ezek. 16:16).

They took other clothing (Ezek. 16:18) and dressed up their images and took YHWH's oil, incense,
and food and offered it to these lifeless fertility idols (cf. Ezek. 16:18-19).

They were so caught up in their commitment and superstition that they sacrificed their own children to Molech
to insure the fertility of land, cattle, and the human population (cf. Ezek. 16:20-21; 20:26,31; 23:37).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 又用你的绣花衣服给他披上，并将我的膏油和香料摆在他跟前；
verses.en: You took your embroidered clothing and used it to cover them; you offered my olive oil and my incense to them.

verses.zh: 又将我赐给你的食物，就是我赐给你吃的细面、油，和蜂蜜，都摆在他跟前为馨香的供物。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: As for my food that I gave you—the fine flour, olive oil, and honey I fed you—you placed it before them as a soothing aroma. That is exactly what happened, declares the Sovereign Lord.
verses.commentary:
16:19 "a soothing aroma" This is an idiomatic way of referring to an accepted sacrifice. Again Ezekiel is
influenced by Leviticus 26, where this terminology is used in a threat (cf. Lev. 26:30-31). Ezekiel uses this idiom
mostly in connection with pagan idolatries (cf. Ezek. 6:13; 16:19; 20:28), however, Ezek. 20:41 is a future-oriented
exception (i.e. the Messianic temple).

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SOOTHING AROMA

verses.zh: 并且你将给我所生的儿女焚献给他。
verses.en: “‘You took your sons and your daughters whom you bore to me and you sacrificed them[NOTE:1] as food for the idols to eat. As if your prostitution was not enough,
notes: The sacrifice of children was prohibited in Lev 18:21; 20:2; Deut 12:31; 18:10.

verses.zh: 你行淫乱岂是小事，竟将我的儿女杀了，使他们经火归与他吗？
verses.en: you slaughtered my children and sacrificed them to the idols.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you gave them, by passing them through to them.” Some believe this alludes to the pagan practice of making children pass through the fire.

verses.zh: 你行这一切可憎和淫乱的事，并未追念你幼年赤身露体滚在血中的日子。
verses.en: And with all your abominable practices and prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, kicking around in your blood.
verses.commentary:
16:22 "you did not remember the days of your youth" The VERB "remember"
(BDB 269, KB 219, Qal PERFECT) occurs twice. Jerusalem's idolatries are
more egregious because

- she was chosen by YHWH

- she was blessed by YHWH

- she was married to YHWH

It was a violation of love as well as law!

verses.zh: 你行这一切恶事之后（主耶和华说：你有祸了！有祸了！）
verses.en: “‘After all your evil—“Woe! Woe to you!” declares the Sovereign Lord—
verses.commentary:
16:23-29 This is a list of the nations with which Judea made political alliances and, thereby, introduced their gods into its culture.

- Egypt, Ezek. 16:26

- Philistia, Ezek. 16:27

- Assyria, Ezek. 16:28

- Babylon, Ezek. 16:29

16:23 "(Woe, woe to you!' declares the Lord God)" This INTERJECTION (BDB 17) implies "grief
and despair to you" (cf. Ezek. 24:6,9). It is used mostly by Jeremiah (cf. Ezek. 4:13,31; 6:4; 10:19; 13:27; 15:10; 45:3; 48:46). There are consequences of
human choices! Infidelity brings a sharp response from a faithful, loving God! Judgment is painful for Judah and for YHWH!

verses.zh: 又为自己建造圆顶花楼，在各街上做了高台。
verses.en: you built yourself a chamber[NOTE:1] and put up a pavilion[NOTE:2] in every public square.
notes: The Hebrew גֶּב (gev) may represent more than one word, each rare in the Old Testament. It may refer to a “mound” or to “rafters.” The LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate interpret this as a brothel.
Or “lofty place” (NRSV). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:229, and B. Lang, Frau Weisheit, 137.
verses.commentary:
16:24

NASB, NKJV
"a shrine. . .a high place"

NRSV
"a platform. . .a lofty place"

TEV
"places to worship"

NJB
"a mound. . .a high place"

REB
"a couch. . .a shrine"

Peshitta
"a house of idols. . .altars"

JPSOA
"an eminence. . .your mound"

LXX
"a house of fornication. . .a public place"

These two terms denote a raised platform.

- "shrine," BDB 146, literally "mound" (in this sense only in this chapter, Ezek. 16:24,31,39)

- "high place," BDB 928, in this chapter (Ezek. 16:24,25,31,39) are the only occurrences of this term in
the sense of a manmade, raised platform. It is used in 1 Sam. 22:6 as a natural height. These same
Hebrew letters (BDB 941 II) form the VERB "to deal treacherously"
(in Piel stem). This might be a wordplay.

- מרום ‒ "high place"

- מרמה ‒ "deal treacherously"

Fertility worship was usually performed on hills, but Israel and Judah moved the worship onto man-made platforms

verses.zh: 因此我伸手攻击你，减少你应用的粮食，又将你交给恨你的非利士众女（众女是城邑的意思；本章下同），使她们任意待你。她们见你的淫行，为你羞耻。
verses.en: So see here, I have stretched out my hand against you and cut off your rations. I have delivered you into the power of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your obscene conduct.
verses.commentary:
16:27 "I have stretched out My hand" This is an idiom for action.

KB 480, Niphal PARTICIPLE) by Judah's idolatry, cf. Ezek. 16:57; 5:14-15; 22:4. Instead of being a
light to the nations Judah was a stumbling block.

The term "lewd" (BDB 273) is a term used several times in Leviticus to denote improper sexual partners
(cf. Lev. 18:17; 19:29; 22:11). This lewdness would result in exile from the Promised Land (cf. Lev. 18:24-30; 20:22-23). Ezekiel
uses this priestly terminology (i.e. he was a priest of the line of Zadok) to shock Judah about her sins (cf. Ezek. 16:27,43,58; 22:9,11;
23:21,27,29,35,44,48[twice],49; 24:13; see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 1113).

verses.en: You engaged in prostitution with the Assyrians because your desires were insatiable; you prostituted yourself with them and yet you were still not satisfied.

notes: Heb “Chaldea.” The name of the tribal group ruling Babylon (“Chaldeans”) and the territory from which they originated (“Chaldea”) are used as metonymy for the whole empire of Babylon.

connotation because of the idolatries of the ten tribes of Canaan. When God's people act like unfair traders, they are characterized as
Canaanites (cf. Hosea 12:8).

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：你行这一切事，都是不知羞耻妓女所行的，可见你的心是何等懦弱！

verses.commentary:
16:30-34 Judah was so desperate for political alliances that she pursued the surrounding nations for help. She never felt
secure (i.e. "never satisfied," cf. Ezek. 16:28,29). She was an unusual harlot in that she paid to be loved (cf. Ezek. 16:41, i.e. protected)!
This is possibly a reference to Tiglath-pileser III being bribed by King Ahaz in 2 Kgs. 16:8.

were found in a hidden room behind the shelves that contained the Scripture scrolls in the synagogue of Cairo, Egypt. These copies have "How
inflamed was your heart," which fits the context much better and may be the source of the Septuagint and Vulgate translations of "how strong" (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 426).

KB (63 II) asserts there is another use of this root in the Qal stem that means "hot with fever."

verses.en: therefore, take note: I am about to gather all your lovers whom you enjoyed, both all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around, and I will expose your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.[NOTE:1]

verses.commentary:
16:37 "I shall gather" This VERB (BDB 867, KB
1062, Piel PARTICIPLE and Piel PERFECT
with waw) is used twice in this verse. It is YHWH who brings the mercenary Neo-Babylonian army into

now part of the Neo-Babylonian army under Nebuchadnezzar II.

The theological tragedy is that this word is often used of YHWH gathering His people as a flock
from exile (cf. Isa. 40:11; Jer. 31:10; Ezek. 34:13; 37:21)but here, because Judah would not repent, her
enemies are gathered to attack her!

▣ "and will leave you naked and bare" The innocent imagery of Ezek. 16:7 has now been replaced
with the violent treatment by the invaders sent by YHWH to punish His unfaithful bride (Ezek. 16:48).

The rabbis developed this contrast between a time of innocence and a time of responsibility by
their theological concept of the two yetzers ("intents"). Until the age of knowledge and commitment
(i.e. Bar Mitzvah, males, age 13 or Bat Mitvah, females, age 12) children were not responsible
for keeping the Law, but after study and vows, they were responsible.

verses.en: “‘Because you did not remember the days of your youth and have enraged me with all these deeds, I hereby repay you for what you have done,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord. Have you not engaged in prostitution on top of all your other abominable practices?

verses.en: You are the daughter of your mother, who detested her husband and her sons, and you are the sister of your sisters, who detested their husbands and their sons. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.

verses.en: Your older sister was Samaria, who lived north[NOTE:1] of you with her daughters, and your younger sister, who lived south[NOTE:2] of you, was Sodom[NOTE:3] with her daughters.
notes: Heb “left.”
Heb “right.”
Sodom was the epitome of evil (Deut 29:23; 32:32; Isa 1:9-10; 3:9; Jer 23:14; Lam 4:6; Matt 10:15; 11:23-24; Jude 7).
verses.commentary:
16:46 This verse specifies that Ezekiel is talking about three sinful capital cities that experienced
the judgment of God.

- Samaria (i.e. Israel), taken captive for her unfaithfulness by Assyria in
722 B.C.

- Sodom (and Gomorrah), destroyed for their wickedness in Genesis 18

- Jerusalem (i.e. Judah), who has been (i.e. 605, 597 B.C.) and would be,
taken captive (i.e. 586 B.C.) by Neo-Babylon (even another exile in
582 B.C.)

This comparison is very similar to chapter 23 (Oholah/Samaria and Oholibah/Jerusalem). Also note
Jer. 3:6-10,11.

▣ "and her daughters" This phrase (cf. Ezek. 16:49,55,57,61) refers to the surrounding villages,
socially and economically connected to these large walled cities.

verses.zh: 你没有效法她们的行为，也没有照她们可憎的事去做，你以那为小事，你一切所行的倒比她们更坏。

Heb “strengthen the hand of.”
verses.commentary:
16:49 In Genesis 19 Sodom is described as a city of sexual deviation (i.e. homosexuality) and is

help, but she would not! YHWH cares for the poor, alien, outcast, orphaned, and socially disenfranchised
(cf. Deut. 10:18; 14:29; 24:17-22; 26:13; 27:19)!

verses.commentary:
16:59 "you who have despised the oath by breaking the covenant" These are serious charges!

- "despised," BDB 102, KB 117, Qal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 17:16,18,19;
Isa. 24:5

- "breaking," BDB 830, KB 924, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

Covenants were confirmed by a sacrifice (i.e. cutting an animal) and an oath of obedience to its
obligations. In the Ancient Near East, breaking an oath (BDB 46)/covenant (BDB 136) resulted in the curses and
negative consequences spelled out in the covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). Israel had reaped
these curses and now Judah!

verses.zh: 然而我要追念在你幼年时与你所立的约，也要与你立定永约。
verses.en: Yet I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish a lasting[NOTE:1] covenant with you.
notes: Or “eternal.”
verses.commentary:
16:60-63 YHWH will remember His covenant and restore His people (cf. Gen. 17:7,19; Lev. 26:11,44-45; Deut. 4:31) because of
His eternal plan of redemption (SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

Notice the reciprocal actions

- God's sovereign choices (notice the number of "I's" like Ezek. 36:22-36).

- "I will remember My covenant with you," Ezek. 16:60, BDB 269, KB 209, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Lev. 26:42,45

- "I will establish an everlasting covenant with you," Ezek. 16:60, BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil PERFECT with waw.
This is referring to the "new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34, which is described in Ezek. 36:22-38

- "when I have forgiven you for all that you have done," Ezek. 16:63, BDB 497, KB 493, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- the covenant people's actions

- you will remember your ways, Ezek. 16:62,63; 20:43; 36:31

- you will be ashamed, Ezek. 16:62,63; 36:32

Both divine initiative and human repentance are required for covenant!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

16:60 "I will establish an everlasting covenant" This is surprising because the Mosaic covenant was
meant to be perpetual. However, it was also conditional on human obedience (as well as a circumcized heart,
cf. Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26; Rom. 2:28-29). It was the inability for obedience
on the part of fallen mankind (cf. Genesis 3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND),
even covenant people, that necessitated a "new" different approach. The "new" covenant would be based on divine performance
(cf. Isaiah 53 and Ezek. 36:22-36). It would provide internal motivation for obedience (cf. Jer. 31:31-34). The contrast can be seen by
comparing Ezek. 18:30-32 with Ezek. 36:26-27.

God still wants a righteous people who will reflect His character to the nations, but now the
focus has shifted from human performance-based covenant to a divine performance-based covenant. Gratitude and
family love replace the wages of a hireling! We serve and obey because we are already accepted! Obedience
is not what makes us accepted, but the evidence that we have been accepted (cf. Eph. 1:4;
2:8-10; James 2:14-26). The goal for new covenant believers is Christlikeness!
